- Only template q16: partsupp JOIN part (filtered: brand<>, type NOT LIKE prefix, size IN 8 consts) + NOT IN (supplier LIKE) mark join, GROUP BY brand,type,size count(DISTINCT suppkey). ~27.8k groups, ~1.18M rows into the agg. - E0005: distinct radix table partitioned on hash(G) only (partition_key_count, gated on estimated_cardinality >= 4096): q16 -12%. Current best is 1.187x.

- Facts: TryPushdownInFilter (filter_combiner.cpp:515) pushes only OptionalFilter(InFilter) unless the list is a dense range. - count(DISTINCT x) GROUP BY G 102-145 ms; SELECT DISTINCT G,x 65 ms; GROUP BY G count(*) 30 ms.
- Chunk compaction is only ~10% of agg CPU and noisy (CACHE_THRESHOLD = 64, physical_operator.hpp:270): a weak lever.

### KEY FINDING R4: the non-inlined VARCHAR key (p_type, 25 chars) costs the aggregate
- DISTINCT on the 4 keys: 46-59 ms (p_type) vs 35 (hash) vs 29 (fixed-width). CompressedMaterialization packs strings up to 16 bytes only. TryAddDictionaryGroups (aggregate_hashtable.cpp:359) handles only a single dictionary group column.

### Exhausted / no-gain (do not repeat)
- E0001 early HT grow ~3%; E0002/E0004 unpartitioned staging for AllConstant layouts ~-1%; E0003 early SkipLookups ≤3%. Sink-side probe/staging tweaks are exhausted.
- Manual 2-level rewrite of count(DISTINCT): same speed.
- Lesson: CPU saved in the distinct sink doesn't show in wall time (it overlaps the join pipeline). Target serial phases: distinct finalize, main re-sink, main finalize, and the build-side pipeline of the join.

### Codebase facts
- Radix HT (radix_partitioned_hashtable.cpp): with more than 2 threads the sink capacity is 32768. Abandon() when full. DecideAdaptation runs at 1M rows per thread. MAXIMUM_FINAL_SINK_RADIX_BITS = 8. CreateHT is at line 71.
- Hash bits: salt = top 16. Radix bits = [48-r, 48), r ≤ 12. Slot = low bits.
- Distinct tables: DistinctAggregateData ctor (distinct_aggregate_data.cpp:75). grouping_set lists the group indices first.
- AggregateDistinctGrouping (physical_hash_aggregate.cpp:666-772): GetData from the distinct radix table, Sink into the main table, then Combine. FinishEvent inserts HashAggregateFinalizeEvent. CanSkipRegularSink is at line 98. partition_key_count is set at line ~201.
- Per-partition finalize: RadixHTLocalSourceState::Finalize (~853).
- InClauseRewriter::VisitReplace (in_clause_rewriter.cpp:35): 1 const → '=', <6 → OR chain, otherwise MARK join. The IN executor loop is in execute_operator.cpp:23 (Equals+Or per constant).
- Perfect HJ: CanDoPerfectHashJoin (perfect_hash_join_executor.cpp:66), MAX_BUILD_SIZE 1M. A perfect HT disables the BF (physical_hash_join.cpp:761), and the BF cuts the partsupp scan from 8M rows to 1.24M, so a perfect HJ is likely a loss for q16.
- dbe-tool: multiple statements per sql call work; grep piping is allowed. Use max(col), not count(*), to keep the distinct agg.

### Backlog (ranked)
1. Main-HT bypass for all-distinct aggs with aligned partitions (filed; high risk, 5-10%).
2. Dictionary-ID substitution for long-string group keys (large).
3. Chunk compaction (weak). Perfect HJ (doubtful because of the BF).

issues.title: Evaluate small integral constant IN lists inline instead of a MARK join
issues.hypothesis: In q16 the part scan emits 1,856,009 rows (0.10s CPU). The pushed `p_size IN (8 consts)` is only an OptionalFilter, used for zonemap pruning (filter_combiner.cpp:580-585). InClauseRewriter::VisitReplace (in_clause_rewriter.cpp:60) turns IN lists with >=6 constants into a MARK join against a COLUMN_DATA_SCAN, followed by a FILTER on the mark column. So every one of the 1.86M part rows is hashed, probed and marked before 84% of them are dropped. All of this happens in the join build pipeline, which has to finish before the partsupp probe pipeline starts, so it sits on the critical path. For a short list of integer constants, a vectorized membership test (a few compares per row, or a bitmap) is much cheaper than a hash-join probe. It also lets the FILTER put the cheap integer predicate ahead of the string predicates (brand <>, NOT LIKE).
issues.plan: 1) src/optimizer/in_clause_rewriter.cpp InClauseRewriter::VisitReplace: before the mark-join path (after the `< 6` check), return nullptr (keep the BoundOperatorExpression COMPARE_IN/NOT_IN unchanged) when all of these hold: children[0]->return_type is an integral physical type of at most 64 bits (INT8..INT64, UINT8..UINT64; no HUGEINT, no DECIMAL needed), every child from 1 on is a non-NULL BoundConstantExpression, and children.size()-1 <= 64. 2) src/execution/expression_executor/execute_operator.cpp: add a fast path to the COMPARE_IN/NOT_IN branch (line 23) for the same condition. Cast the constants to int64 (or to the physical type), then evaluate the left vector with UnifiedVectorFormat. If max-min < 4096, test with a bitmap (vector<bool>/bitset built per call, or cached in ExpressionState if simple); otherwise use a sorted array with binary search. Write a BOOLEAN result that is NULL where the left side is NULL and true/false (inverted for NOT IN) otherwise. Keep the existing generic loop for everything else. Make sure the Select path (filter) goes through this Execute path or add a Select specialization. Check that the FILTER over part.p_size now evaluates IN directly and that the MARK join is gone from the q16 EXPLAIN.
issues.expected_gain: q16 3-6% wall: removes a 1.86M-row mark-join probe and its hash from the serial build-side pipeline (scan+filter+mark ~0.13s+ CPU).
issues.generality: Any query with a filter or projection of the form int_col [NOT] IN (6..64 integer constants), which is very common in TPC-H/DS-style workloads (sizes, years, ids). Lists with more than 64 values, non-integral types and non-constant lists keep the mark join. Possible slowdown: a 64-value list with a wide range uses binary search, which is still cheaper than a hash probe.
issues.risk: Low-medium. NULL semantics: left NULL gives NULL. Constants are non-NULL by the gate, so NOT IN has no NULL-in-list edge case. Integer constants must already be cast to the left type (the binder does this); assert or bail out if the types differ.

issues.title: Bypass main HT for all-distinct aggregates with group-aligned distinct partitions
issues.hypothesis: After E0005 every distinct radix partition holds complete groups, but AggregateDistinctGrouping (physical_hash_aggregate.cpp:666-772) still re-sinks every distinct tuple (1.18M) into a local main HT, then runs Combine and HashAggregateFinalizeEvent. HASH_GROUP_BY is still 0.45-0.73s CPU, and in the R5 temp-table test re-aggregation cost ~40 ms wall of ~150.
issues.plan: When partition_key_count is set and CanSkipRegularSink() holds, have each distinct-finalize task keep a local main HT per distinct partition sized to that partition. Skip the global combine by writing the finalized groups directly into a per-partition result collection that the main source scans.
issues.generality: GROUP BY queries whose aggregates are all DISTINCT
issues.risk: High: large change to the source and finalize state machine.
